item.title:
A new HOA board should inherit more than folders. It should inherit the reasons behind major decisions, the status of professional recommendations, the history of building systems, the promises vendors made, and the work that still needs attention. Board turnover is normal. Reconstructing the association from old emails every two years should not be. Steward helps preserve a searchable, source-linked history so incoming directors can ask, "Why did we do this?" and see the records behind the answer. What does your association's handoff actually include?

item.description: The board changed. Did the memory leave too?

item.title:
"Everything is in Dropbox" sounds reassuring - until someone asks why the roof project changed, whether the engineer's recommendation was completed, or what the previous board promised owners. Documents can exist while the story remains scattered. Institutional memory means connecting the minutes, reports, contracts, invoices, emails, and decisions well enough that the next board can understand what happened. That is the problem Steward was built to solve.
#HOABoard #CommunityAssociation #BoardGovernance #HOAManagement #InstitutionalKnowledge
item.description: A folder is not institutional memory

item.title:
"I think the previous board handled that." Maybe it did. Maybe it discussed the issue but never voted. Maybe it approved a repair but not the full replacement. Maybe the vendor recommended follow-up that never happened. Memory is not an audit trail. Before repeating work - or repeating a mistake - boards need a fast way to find the underlying record. Steward lets an association ask questions across its own documents and trace the answer back to the source.

item.title:
Volunteer directors change. Managers change. Vendors change. The association's obligations do not. Warranties, inspection findings, reserve assumptions, contracts, claims, and prior decisions must remain usable long after the person who filed them is gone. The Foundation for Community Association Research calls for structured transitions and centralized institutional records. Steward makes that principle practical for everyday board work.
#HOABoard #CommunityAssociation #BoardTransition #InstitutionalKnowledge #HOAManagement
item.description: Your records should outlast your board

item.title:
Most incoming HOA directors receive a governing-document binder, a budget, access to a portal, and a flood of acronyms. What they rarely receive is context: Why assessments changed. Which projects were deferred. What the reserve specialist warned about. Which contracts are approaching renewal. What owners were already told. New directors do not need more documents. They need a way to understand them. That is the difference between storage and continuity.
